ops.title: desk-runner flush no longer rewrites the action store for already-held deferred escalations (long-running 0.7.207)
ops.body:
PR #562 (merge 2bcacba8, tag long-running--v0.7.207). Runner.flush snapshots the runner incident's deferred-escalations IDs once per pass (after release_deferred) and calls Runner.defer only for a deferrable escalation not already held.

Why: defer -> Book.edit -> actions.Store.owned rewrites the whole store on exit even when hold() changes nothing. A live orca desk-runner (long-running 0.7.190, store 7,370,616 bytes, 16 accepted RECLAIM/DEADLINE escalations all already held) did 16 full-store rewrites per 10 s pass: a predicted 11.25 MiB/s against 11.26 MiB/s of process-accounted writes. The duplicate writes are proven from source; per-file attribution of the sample is a rate fit.

Remaining pattern: Store.owned has no equality check, so any other Book.edit whose change is a no-op still rewrites the full store. The finder review found no other recurring no-op write inside flush/defer.

Activation: runners started from 0.7.207 carry the fix. A runner already running keeps the code it loaded; there is no in-process reload (desk-runner `handoff` replaces the process). Regression: tests/test_desk_runner.py::test_an_escalation_already_held_for_the_incident_leaves_the_store_unwritten_on_later_passes.
